### Answer
Jeff McMahon was a key figure in Enron's finance leadership, holding two significant roles during the period of interest. Initially, he served as the Treasurer of Enron Corp, reporting to Andrew Fastow from January 1, 1998, to March 1, 2001. Later, he took on the role of Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of Enron Corp, reporting directly to Kenneth Lay from October 25, 2001, to January 28, 2002.

The change in his role was significant during the 2001 crisis. McMahon's transition from Treasurer to CFO occurred amidst Enron's financial turmoil. As Treasurer, he reported to Andrew Fastow, who was later implicated in Enron's financial scandals.
